Each hour: time, direction and speed (knots, g = gust), odds of 12kt or more, regime, waves, tide height in ft with r rising or f falling. OUTFLOW NOT RIDDEN = Squamish outflow, never recommend. OFF DIR = direction does not work at that spot.
Riding light (first light to last light, Vancouver): Sat, Oct 24 7:14am to 6:38pm; Sun, Oct 25 7:16am to 6:36pm; Mon, Oct 26 7:17am to 6:34pm. Hours outside that are dark and not listed; never suggest riding then.

Guillermo's own take for Sat, Oct 24 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Easterly Saturday. Sand Heads already reads E 14 at 5am and Point Atkinson ESE 11, a few knots ahead of the page, and Environment Canada calls 15 to 20 this afternoon.

I think we may run out of light, but Boundary Bay from about 1:30pm is a possibility. The page shows ENE 9 to 11, and the tide peaks at 13.2ft at 4:30pm, so plenty of water.

At Porteau, Pam Rocks forecast reaches 21, which is usually short of what it needs to fire up Porteau, but worth monitoring. Erwin Park usually works on an easterly, so worth monitoring too, but the forecast on this site disagrees today.

Tomorrow looks like a strong Porteau outflow: 28 at 10am, 84%.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 10:30 AM PDT 24 October 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Sunday. Gale warning in effect. Wind northerly outflow 10 to 15 knots increasing to northerly outflow 15 to 25 early this evening and to northerly outflow 30 to 40 late overnight. Wind diminishing to northerly outflow 20 to 30 near noon Sunday.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 10:30 AM PDT 24 October 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Sunday. Strong wind warning in effect. Wind easterly 10 to 20 knots becoming easterly 15 to 25 this evening then becoming easterly 10 to 20 Sunday afternoon. Wind becoming northerly 10 Sunday evening.
